entities.name: Leonhard von Keutschach
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Leonhard von Keutschach was Prince-Archbishop of Salzburg from 1495 until his death on June 18, 1519, marking the last time a ruler governed in the feudal style in the region.

As the Archbishop of Salzburg, von Keutschach played a significant role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various territories.

Von Keutschach's tenure was also marked by his efforts to promote the arts and architecture in Salzburg, including the construction of the stunning Salzburger Dom, a masterpiece of Gothic architecture that still stands today.

In the centuries following his death, the legacy of von Keutschach continued to shape the cultural and religious landscape of Salzburg, leaving behind a lasting impact on the region's history and identity.
